facts.statement: Laquintasaura is the genus name for this extinct dinosaur.
facts.quote: genus: Laquintasaura

facts.statement: The only known species is Laquintasaura venezuelae.
facts.quote: species: venezuelae

facts.statement: The genus was formally described by Barrett and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Barrett et al., 2014

facts.statement: Laquintasaura is considered one of the most primitive ornithischians and the first dinosaur identified from Venezuela.
facts.quote: It is known for being one of the most primitive ornithischians in the fossil record, as well as the first dinosaur to have been identified from Venezuela.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the La Quinta Formation with the Greek suffix for lizard.
facts.quote: The name is derived from the La Quinta Formation, where it was discovered, and the feminine Greek suffix for lizard

facts.statement: The species is known from hundreds of fossil elements found in a single extensive bonebed.
facts.quote: It is known from hundreds of fossil elements, all derived from a single extensive bonebed locality.

facts.statement: The site was initially discovered by French paleontologists, with subsequent excavations largely led by Marcelo R Sánchez-Villagra.
facts.quote: Initially discovered by French palaeontologists, numerous expeditions have been conducted to excavate from the bonebed, largely led by Marcelo R Sánchez-Villagra.

facts.statement: Remains were initially attributed to Lesothosaurus before being formally named Laquintasaura in 2014.
facts.quote: Once thought to represent remains of Lesothosaurus, it was formally named in a 2014 study

facts.statement: It was a small, lightly built animal not exceeding 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: A small animal, it is thought to have been a lightly built and would not have grown much larger than 1 m in length.

facts.statement: It possessed a bird-like hip bone and was likely a capable bipedal runner.
facts.quote: One of the first species known to possess the distinctive bird-like hip bone of ornithischians, it would have been a capable bipedal runner.

facts.statement: Its teeth were triangular with striations and sharp denticles, unlike the leaf-shaped teeth of related ornithischians.
facts.quote: Unlike the leaf shaped teeth of related ornithschians, those of Laquintasaura had a distinctive triangular shape, with distinct striations and sharp denticles running down the edges.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest its unique teeth may have supported an omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: These may have contributed to an omnivorous diet unlike those of later relatives.

facts.statement: It likely lived in groups on seasonal alluvial plains and was preyed upon by Tachiraptor.
facts.quote: They would have lived in groups, living on a seasonal alluvial plain and being preyed upon by the contemporary Tachiraptor.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether it is an early diverging ornithischian or belongs to the subgroup Thyreophora.
facts.quote: Taxonomic uncertainty has led to conflicting hypotheses that it is either an early diverging ornithischian or part of the subgroup Thyreophora.

facts.statement: The fossils come from a single bonebed in the Early Jurassic La Quinta Formation.
facts.quote: Laquintasaura is known from a single locality, a bonebed in rocks of the La Quinta Formation, which is Early Jurassic in age.

facts.statement: The bonebed was discovered in the 1980s by French paleontologists near La Grita and Seboruco in the state of Táchira, Venezuela.
facts.quote: This bonebed was first discovered in the 1980s by a team of French palaeontologists on a reconnaissance mission to Venezuela, near a road between the towns of La Grita and Seboruco, in the state of Táchira.

facts.statement: The initial French discovery included two teeth and a fragment of a quadrate bone.
facts.quote: Initially, the French team discovered two teeth and the fragment of a quadrate (a bone at the back of the skull, articulating with the jaw).

facts.statement: The initial fossils were described by D.E. Russell and colleagues in 1992.
facts.quote: described by D.E. Russel and colleagues in a 1992 publication.

facts.statement: The initial fossils were tentatively assigned to the genus Lesothosaurus without a specific species name.
facts.quote: Based on similar cranial anatomy, they were tentatively referred to the genus Lesothosaurus but not to any specific species

facts.statement: Sánchez-Villagra and colleagues conducted expeditions in 1992 and 1993 after an initial 1989 survey.
facts.quote: Marcelo R. Sánchez-Villagra and colleagues conducted their own expeditions into the La Quinta Formation in 1992 and 1993 following an initial survey in 1989.

facts.statement: A successful expedition in December 1993 produced abundant new material.
facts.quote: A successful trip was organized in December 1993 with a new team from Caracas, which produced abundant new material.

facts.statement: The abundant material was formally described in a 2014 paper by Barrett, Sánchez-Villagra, and colleagues.
facts.quote: This additional material was described in a 2014 paper by a team including Barrett and Sánchez-Villagra.

facts.statement: The holotype is tooth MBLUZ P.1396, with paratypes including a partial femur, partial left ischium, and left astragalocalcaneum.
facts.quote: Among the material, the isolated tooth MBLUZ P.1396 was designated as the holotype, forming the type series with paratypes MBLUZ P.5017, a partial femur; MBLUZ P.5018, a partial left ischium; and MBLUZ P.5005, a left astragalocalcaneum.

facts.statement: A premaxilla was described in a 2021 study by Herrera-Castillo, Sánchez-Villagra, and colleagues.
facts.quote: A later 2021 study by Carlos-Manuel Herrera-Castillo, Sánchez-Villagra, and colleagues described a premaxilla that has been prepared and studied since the 2014 paper

facts.statement: Hundreds of fossil elements represent at least four individuals, possibly more.
facts.quote: Hundreds of individual fossil elements are known for Laquintasaura, representing a minimum of four individuals and potentially many more.

facts.statement: Prepared material included cranial remains, abundant teeth, various vertebrae, a scapula, and pelvic and hindlimb elements.
facts.quote: Material that had already been prepared upon publication of the 2014 paper included isolated cranial remains, an abundance of teeth, cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae, a scapula, pelvic and hindlimb material, and other isolated postcranial elements.

facts.statement: Forelimb material was completely absent and foot material was very limited.
facts.quote: Forelimb material was completely absent, and material from the feet was very limited.

facts.statement: Similar dental morphotypes found in India and England date to the Middle Jurassic, over 30 million years after Laquintasaura lived.
facts.quote: Dental morphotypes similar to that of Laquintasaura have been described from the Kota Formation in India as well as from the White Limestone Formation in England. They date to the Bathonian age of the Middle Jurassic, more than 30 million years after Laquintasaura lived.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura is assumed to have been a lithe bipedal animal.
facts.quote: Like other early members of Ornithischia, it is assumed that Laquintasaura was a lithe bipedal animal.

facts.statement: The largest femur found in the Laquintasaura bonebed measures 90 mm in length.
facts.quote: The largest femur among the bonebed is 90 mm in length

facts.statement: Based on femur proportions, a Laquintasaura individual was estimated to grow to around 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: it was estimated the Laquintasaura individual could grow to around 1 m in length

facts.statement: The most distinctive anatomical feature of Laquintasaura is its dentition.
facts.quote: The most distinctive anatomy of Laquintasaura is found in its dentition.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura teeth are unusually tall with their widest point immediately above the root, forming an isosceles triangle shape.
facts.quote: The teeth are unusually tall and have their widest point immediately above the tooth root; the result of this is an isoceles triangle shape.

facts.statement: Unlike later ornithischians, Laquintasaura had uniform dental anatomy throughout the entire mouth, including the premaxilla and maxilla.
facts.quote: As opposed to the heterodont condition of later ornithischians, this dental anatomy is thought to have been uniform throughout the entirety of the mouth, both in the premaxilla and the maxilla.

facts.statement: The upper surface of the Laquintasaura ischium, above the obturator process, is highly inflected.
facts.quote: The upper surface of the ischium further up than the obturator process is highly inflected

facts.statement: The epicondyle connecting the femur and fibula in Laquintasaura is inset in the middle when viewed from below or behind.
facts.quote: The epicondyle at the connection of the femur and the fibula is inset in the middle from a ventral or posterior view

facts.statement: Laquintasaura is the oldest known ornithischian with a backward-pointing pubis.
facts.quote: They brought attention to the backward-pointing pubis, as Laquintasaura is the oldest known ornithischian with this trait

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Laquintasaura were found in a bonebed containing a femur 90 mm long.
facts.quote: The largest femur among the bonebed is 90 mm in length

facts.statement: Laquintasaura is robustly considered a basal member of Ornithischia, though its exact position within the group remains unresolved.
facts.quote: It is robustly considered a basal member of the group Ornithischia, but its exact position within this clade are unresolved.

facts.statement: Some 2017 studies suggested Laquintasaura was a very early member of Thyreophora, as the sister taxon to Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: Some studies, such as that of Matthew G. Baron and David Norman or that of Thomas J. Raven and Susannah Maidment, both in 2017, have found it to be a very early member of the group Thyreophora (armored dinosaurs), as the sister taxon of Scutellosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2022 study placed Laquintasaura outside Prionodontia, intermediate between traditional Ornithischia and Silesauridae.
facts.quote: Similarly, a 2022 study by Baron, Norman, and colleagues found it to be outside of the clade Prionodontia (known Saphornithischia under alternative nomenclatural schemes), intermediate between the traditional scope of Ornithischia and a grade of animals that traditionally compose Silesauridae.

facts.statement: Bone histology analysis suggested one Laquintasaura tibia belonged to a juvenile approximately three years old.
facts.quote: Based on the presence of only two annuli, growth indicating rings, it was determined that the tibia likely belong to a juvenile around three years old.

facts.statement: Analysis of a scapula indicated it belonged to a mature Laquintasaura adult likely around ten to twelve years old.
facts.quote: Contrastingly, the presence of at least nine tightly spaced lines of arrested growth and extensive bone remodelling in the scapula indicated it belonged to a mature adult, likely around ten to twelve years of age.

facts.statement: All examined Laquintasaura specimens lack fibrolamellar bone tissue, which is associated with high growth rates in other ornithischians.
facts.quote: It was noted that all of the specimens lack fibrolamellar bone tissue, associated with high growth rates in ornithischians such as Lesothosaurus, ornithopods, and marginocephalians.

facts.statement: Conclusions about Laquintasaura's growth rates remain uncertain due to limited data and sample size.
facts.quote: However, due to the lack of data on ornithischian histology as a whole, as well as the limited sample size available to confirm the lack of that tissue organization in Laquintasaura, these conclusions remain uncertain.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura fossils were found in the Venezuelan part of the La Quinta Formation, an area now spanning Colombia and Venezuela.
facts.quote: Laquintasaura hails from the La Quinta Formation in what is now Colombia and Venezuela, found in the Venezuelan part of the formation.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura venezuelae is a Venezuelan ornithischian dinosaur genus containing only the type species L. venezuelae.
facts.quote: Laquintasaura venezuelae es un género de dinosaurio ornitisquio venezolano que contiene solo la especie tipo Laquintasaura venezuelae.

facts.statement: L. venezuelae was the first dinosaur species identified in Venezuela.
facts.quote: La especie fue el primer dinosaurio identificado en Venezuela.

facts.statement: The species is known from extensive remains found in a single bonebed site sampled during expeditions largely led by Marcelo R Sánchez-Villagra.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de extensos restos, todos de una localidad de lecho óseo singular que ha sido muestreada en busca de bloques de especímenes en el transcurso de varias expediciones, en gran parte dirigidas por Marcelo R Sánchez-Villagra.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura is a small, very primitive animal known for its distinct dental anatomy and status as one of the oldest and most primitive ornithischians in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Un animal pequeño y muy primitivo, es conocido por su anatomía dental distinta y por ser uno de los ornitisquios más antiguos y primitivos del registro fósil.

facts.statement: Taxonomic uncertainty has led to contradictory theories that Laquintasaura is either the base of Ornithischia or the base of the suborder Thyreophora.
facts.quote: La incertidumbre taxonómica ha llevado a teorías contradictorias de que es la base de Ornithischia o la base del subgrupo Thyreophora.

facts.statement: Researcher Paul Barrett described Laquintasaura venezuelae as a small, dog-sized animal that walked on its two hind legs.
facts.quote: El investigador Paul Barrett, del Museo de Historia Natural de Londres, describió que Laquintasaura venezuelae caminaba sobre sus dos patas traseras y era del tamaño de un perro pequeño.

facts.statement: The largest femur found was 90 mm long, suggesting the bipedal dinosaur was about 1 meter long and 25 cm high at the hips.
facts.quote: El mayor fémur encontrado fue de 90 milímetros de largo, lo que sugiere que todo el cuerpo del dinosaurio bípedo fue de aproximadamente 1 metro de largo y 25 centímetros de alto en la cadera.

facts.statement: Laquintasaura likely lived in an alluvial plain ecosystem characterized by both arid and humid seasons.
facts.quote: The ecosystem that Laquintasaura lived in is thought to represent an alluvial plain, with both arid and humid seasons.

facts.statement: The early theropod dinosaur Tachiraptor likely lived alongside Laquintasaura and preyed upon it.
facts.quote: The early theropod dinosaur Tachiraptor would have lived alongside Laquintasaura, and likely preyed upon it.

facts.statement: While the dinosaur's diet consisted mainly of ferns, its dental structure suggests it could have fed on insects and small prey.
facts.quote: Si bien la dieta del dinosaurio consistía principalmente de helechos, la conformación de su dentadura sugiere que pudo alimentarse de insectos y de pequeñas presas.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of L. venezuelae possesses 7 teeth and lacks a diastema near the premaxilla-maxilla suture.
facts.quote: La premaxila de L. venezuelae posee 7 dientes y no presenta un diastema cercano a la sutura premaxilo-maxilar.
